title: Maximum Consecutive Floors Without Special Floors
summary: Alice has rented floors from the bottom to the top inclusive.
statement: Alice has rented floors from the bottom to the top inclusive. She has also designated some of these floors as special, intended for relaxation only. You are provided with the integers bottom and top to define the range of floors Alice has rented, and an array special containing the floor numbers that are designated as special. Determine the maximum number of consecutive floors that do not have any special floor designation.
constraints: Rented floors are every integer from bottom through top inclusive.
Each distinct special floor breaks a consecutive non-special run.
Return the maximum number of consecutive non-special floors, allowing a run at either boundary.
hints: Sort the special floors and add virtual special sentinels just outside the rented range.
The non-special run between two adjacent special markers has length right-left-1.
Every ordinary floor belongs to exactly one gap between consecutive markers, including boundary gaps represented by the sentinels.
editorial: Every ordinary floor belongs to exactly one gap between consecutive markers, including boundary gaps represented by the sentinels.

tests.explanation: The runs are floors 2-3, floor 5, and floors 7-9, so the maximum length is three.
Either boundary run contains one non-special floor.
